factual_claims.claim: Recursive training of generative models on their own output leads to 'model collapse,' a degenerative process where models lose information about the true data distribution.
Model collapse occurs in LLMs, VAEs, and GMMs, suggesting it is a universal phenomenon among generative models.
Training a single moderately large model produces twice the American lifetime's worth of CO2.
The OPT-125m model fine-tuned on wikitext2 with real data achieves a mean perplexity of 34, compared to a zero-shot baseline of 115.
Training with generated data allows models to adapt to the underlying task but results in performance degradation, increasing perplexity from 20 to 28 points in the five-epoch setting.
Preserving 10% of original training data leads to only minor degradation of performance in recursive training settings.
Enforcing a repeating penalty of 2.0 in LLM experiments causes models to perform even worse, with perplexity doubling compared to the original.
